title: Rapid tiling PRD cribsheet
content:
Quick brain-dump / rough PRD sketch for a small compositional feature: 'tiling' as a client-configurable response composition primitive. Intended to be a lightweight, low-risk addition for teams that want to stitch multiple model outputs or microresponses into a coherent final answer without adding latency or complicated orchestration on the client side.

Context and motivation:
- Many product teams want to combine short specialized responses (search snippets, tool outputs, small code transforms) with a final natural-language synthesis step. Today customers either: 1) run multiple independent calls and stitch in-app, increasing round trips and client complexity, or 2) send a single large prompt with many instructions which is brittle and expensive.
- Goal: provide a server-side composition primitive that executes short micro-inferences in parallel/series as appropriate and returns a single merged response. Reduce round trips, keep latency predictable, and enable per-piece routing/cost controls.

High-level proposal:
- Introduce a new request shape: "tiling" request. Top-level payload includes an ordered list of tiles. Each tile defines: model (or model alias/variant), prompt template (string or ref), max_tokens, run_mode (sync|async|prefetch), and a merge policy (concatenate|summarize|slot_merge|json_schema).
- The runtime will attempt to schedule tiles under a single API call: small tiles can be executed concurrently (if model and resources allow), longer tiles can be queued with a per-request budget. The server merges according to merge policy and returns one response stream.

Key user stories:
- As a product engineer I want to run a search snippet tile (cheaper embed+rerank) then ask a synthesis tile (larger model) to compose the snippets into a final answer, without two client round trips.
- As an ML infra engineer I want tiles to be routable to different deployment tiers (dedicated vs hosted) and to fall back to cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained.
- As a privacy-conscious customer I want certain tiles to be marked private-only (run in Private deployment) while others use hosted models; the platform should support mixed routing with user-visible latency/cost tradeoffs.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Decrease average client-side stitching calls for participating beta customers by 60% (measure by SDK telemetry).
- Mean 95th percentile end-to-end latency (tiling requests) <= single-call baseline + 120ms for typical two-tile pattern.
- Beta customers report >30% reduction in host-incurred token bill when moving from naive single-large-prompt to tiled composition (due to targeted model selection and short tile prompts).

Non-goals:
- Not aiming to be a full workflow engine (no long-running stateful DAGs).
- Not replacing full orchestration in Dedicated for complex multi-step data transforms. Keep feature surface intentionally small.

Technical considerations / constraints:
- Scheduling: implement a lightweight tile scheduler in the request front-end. It should decide concurrency based on model compatibility (same GPU backend), memory/KV cache reuse opportunities, and per-request latency budget.
- KV cache reuse: when tiles target the same model version, reuse KV caches where possible to avoid expensive re-encoding. Expose an option in tile spec (allow_kv_reuse: true|false).
- Streaming semantics: support streaming final merged output. For some merge policies (concatenate) we can stream per-tile chunks as they finish. For summarization or slot_merge we may need to wait for all inputs before streaming synthesis. Provide clear event markers in the stream (e.g., tile_start/tile_end/merge_start).
- Failures and graceful degradation: per-tile failure policies: fail-request | skip-tile | replace-with-fallback-tile. Default to skip-tile with a short placeholder note in the merged result. Track per-tile error telemetry for troubleshooting.
- Cost visibility: Console should show per-tile token counts and estimated cost breakdown (model, tokens, compute). This ties into Optimize suggestions (e.g., swap tile model to quantized variant).
- Routing and security: Respect per-tenant routing policies. For mixed-private requests, annotate response with which tiles ran in private environments (and include minimal latency metadata).

API sketch (prototype):
POST /v1/tiling
{
  "request_id": "opt-1234",
  "tiles": [
    {"id":"t1","model":"small-reranker-v1","prompt":"{{query}} -> top5","max_tokens":40,"run_mode":"prefetch","merge":"slot_list"},
    {"id":"t2","model":"redwood-synth-2","prompt":"synthesize snippets: {{t1.output}}","max_tokens":250,"merge":"summarize"}
  ],
  "latency_budget_ms": 350,
  "merge_options": {"summarize_style":"concise"},
  "fail_policy":"skip-tile"
}

UX and console changes (lightweight):
- Add a "Tiling" tab to the Console request inspector where devs can replay the composed tiles, see per-tile timing and token breakdown, and toggle simulated fallbacks.
- Provide a toggle to 'show tile provenance' in the audit logs for compliance.

Rollout plan / phased approach:
1) Internal prototype behind feature flag: support only two-tile patterns and concatenate/summarize merge policies; limited models (hosted catalog small + large synth). Telemetry baked in.
2) Beta: invited customers, expose full tile shape, add streaming markers and console visuals. Collect cost/latency metrics.
3) General availability: add per-tile routing controls, prefetch modes, KV reuse, and Optimize integrations.

Risks & mitigations:
- Increased platform complexity (scheduler + merging): keep the prototyped scheduler rule-based and opt into feature flag. Reject feature creep (no DAGs).
- SLO regressions from parallel scheduling: enforce conservative concurrency defaults and circuit-breakers per-tenant.
- Security/compliance for mixed execution: require explicit tenant opt-in; surface tile execution locations in audit logs.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Merge policies: slot_merge for structured slots needs a safe validation step (schema enforcement). Who owns validator? Research/Applied ML team.
- Cost accounting: how to price multi-tile request? Sum tokens + small per-tiling surcharge? Product to propose.
- SDK ergonomics: helper builders for common patterns (search+compose, toolchain+summarize). UX to design snippets for JS/Python.
- Edge use case: can a tiny tile be executed at edge or in a Local runtime? Explore later.

Immediate next steps (short checklist):
- Sync with serving-runtime to validate KV reuse feasibility (Ishaan).
- Prototype API + scheduler mock server in the SDK for internal dogfood (me: Talia).
- Design simple Console inspector view mock (Mika).
- Draft pricing suggestion for multi-tile accounting (product ops).

Notes to self / heuristics for the beta:
- Limit beta to patterns where downstream synthesis tile depends on a small structured list of snippets (easy merge).
- Default concurrency to 2 tiles in parallel; avoid large fanouts until we have perf data.
- Capture a synthetic workload with a few partners (search-assistant, code-assist) to measure real savings.

Parking lot ideas for later:
- Tile caching across requests (cache tile outputs keyed by prompt+context).
- Declarative 'tile libraries' that teams can store and reuse (templates).
- Visual tile composer in Console (drag/drop).

End of cribsheet — rough, intentionally terse. Planning to flesh into a short PRD and a one-page engineering spec once we validate feasibility with runtime.

-- Talia B.
